title: Form requirements that survive when a written prescription is permitted
rule_summary: Where state and federal law permit a WRITTEN prescription, 105 CMR 721.020(F) requires it to be issued on a form carrying the practitioner's signature and to be EITHER transmitted via facsimile or similar technology OR written on a TAMPER-RESISTANT FORM consistent with federal requirements for Medicaid. M.G.L. c. 94C, s. 23(i) states the same at statute level. Under 105 CMR 721.040(A) a prescription in a format that does not conform is INVALID AND SHALL NOT BE FILLED. An exception that permits a written prescription therefore removes the electronic-format mandate only; the written form requirements continue to govern the prescription the exception allows.
exam_relevance: Tests whether the candidate keeps the electronic-prescribing exception separate from the form requirements that still govern the written prescription it permits.
exceptions: The facsimile route and the tamper-resistant form route are alternatives; either satisfies 105 CMR 721.020(F)(1)-(2).
common_confusions: Reading an electronic-prescribing exception as removing every format requirement rather than the electronic mandate alone.
Filling a written prescription that conforms to no permitted format, when 105 CMR 721.040(A) makes it invalid.
verification_notes: 105 CMR 721.020(F) and 721.040(A) read verbatim in the current official publication dated 9/27/24, and M.G.L. c. 94C, s. 23(i) on malegislature.gov, both on 2026-09-10. Added because the GPT-FRESH-B4-SG-REPAIR-V4 audit found the guide had no canonical home for the form requirement that survives an electronic-prescribing exception. Independent audit still required.
